Lutrin does not collect, transmit or sell any data.
The app does not ask for the permission to access the internet: it technically cannot send anything. You can check it in the information of the app or in the manifest published with the source code.
No ads, no trackers, no telemetry, no remote crash reports.

The only data saved is saved on your device: the list of recent documents and their thumbnails, the last reading position, the preferences, and (from version 1.1) the local history of the actions requested by an assistant, without any document content. You can erase them from the settings or by uninstalling the app.

The passwords of protected PDFs are never saved or offered to password managers. A protected document appears in the recent list (name, page reached) without a thumbnail of its first page, and its password is asked again each time it is opened.
The app only accesses the files you choose (system picker, “Open with”, sharing).
The external links of a document are only opened after your confirmation, by another app (a browser) that you choose.
AI assistants (version 1.1)

If you use an assistant (for example Gemini) to drive Lutrin, the assistant receives the answers of Lutrin and may pass them on to an online service, according to its own privacy policy. For this reason:
reading the content of documents by an assistant is turned off by default;
access by assistants can be turned off entirely in the settings;
the password of a PDF is never asked for or passed on through an assistant.
